messages:
jamie: Heads-up — reproducible KV-cache correctness issue during long-context perf runs. After ~10–12k tokens I'm seeing stale KV blocks get served to subsequent requests (cross-request contamination). Repro steps and logs below.

neha: ugh. does it reproduce with the standalone runner or only in the pooled runtime?

jamie: standalone runner with small concurrency reproduces reliably. Stress script: `scripts/long_ctx_stress.sh` (attached).

jamie: minimal repro command: `LD_PRELOAD=./build/libredwood_kv.so ./bin/runtime --kv-pages=4096 --max-tokens=14000 --seed=42 ./tests/long_context_prompt.json`

oliver: can you paste the snippet of the evidence? logs or mismatch diff helps.

jamie: pasted log excerpt:

```
[2026-03-17T14:02:12Z] request id=0x7f8a kv_page=312 header_tag=0x5b2f cache_block_id=4892
[2026-03-17T14:02:12Z] request id=0x7f8a append token_index=4095 page_offset=4095 -> wrote block start=4096
[2026-03-17T14:02:12Z] request id=0x7f8b kv_page=312 header_tag=0x4a9d cache_block_id=4892 (unexpected)
[2026-03-17T14:02:12Z] request id=0x7f8b served stale block tag=0x5b2f
```

jamie: note tag mismatch — the header_tag expected 0x4a9d for the new request but block 4892 still carries 0x5b2f from previous request.

kate: that looks like a header/tag not being updated on wrap or when we split an append across page boundary. Could be off-by-one in compute_page_index or in update_header() after partial writes.

oliver: i dug into alloc/path: the alignment math is funky when token lengths vary. suspect code at kv_manager.cpp:calc_block_start() when we align by 64-byte slab vs token_count. If append crosses page boundary we shift the "next_slot" incorrectly.

jamie: here's the tiny failing test we added:

```
TEST(KVCache, AppendCrossBoundaryPreservesTag) {
  KvCache c(4096); // pages
  auto a = c.appendTokens(4094); // almost full page
  c.appendTokens(4); // crosses to next page, should allocate new block with new tag
  EXPECT_NE(c.blockForRequest(1).tag, c.blockForRequest(0).tag);
}
```

neha: failing on CI? we didn't catch because most unit tests use small contexts. nice find.

perf-bot: [perf-alert] memory delta per-request on long-context stress: +2.9MB/request over 1k requests (leak-like growth); correlates with increased cache hit of stale blocks.

jamie: local bisect points to commit 58a7c9d — that one changed the page_split path to avoid copying on small appends. suspect we forgot to clear metadata on the moved fragment.

oliver: quick patch idea — after split, explicitly set new_block->header.tag = next_tag(); and increment generation. Also set new_block->owner_req = current_request_id.

kate: would that mask the real bug (misaligned offsets) though? Might hide root cause. We should add asserts to ensure page_offset < page_size and that append length != 0 before reusing block.

jamie: agreed. i'll open a draft PR with a test and two fixes: (1) stricter assert + invariant check in debug, (2) conservative metadata clear on split (for release).

neha: logging suggestion — add short telemetry on per-page last_write_req and last_write_token_index. It's cheap and will help detect cross-request reuse in prod without heavy tracing.

oliver: repro note: tokenizer variability matters. If tokens are short (spaces + punctuation) we hit the boundary differently. Reproduces much less reliably with BPE vs SentencePiece.

kate: actions:
- jamie: PR with failing test + conservative fix (ETA today)
- oliver: add debug-only invariants and runtime assert (ETA tomorrow)
- neha: add perf telemetry config flag and run stress with different tokenizers (ETA tomorrow)

jamie: PR opened: https://git.redwood/redwood/infra/+/D1234 - includes failing test and metadata-clear patch. pls review.

neha: reviewed, left one comment about keeping non-release asserts behind #ifndef NDEBUG.

perf-bot: [ci] long_context_stress: 12 runs completed, 11 failed (repro rate ~92%)

oliver: after jamie's patch measured stable: 1/12 failures. Seems improved but still flaky. I'll instrument the split path to dump the alignment math on failures.

jamie: thanks all. keeping this thread active until we get 0 repros on 100 runs. If anyone sees similar in dedicated runtime please ping — might be sensitive to different page sizes / reserved pools.

kate: FYI I'm adding a canary check to rollout that looks for any requests that served a block with mismatched tag header. Bail and fall back to re-eval the request on mismatch. Safer while we finish fix. :shield:

jamie: thumbs up. updated the PR to include the canary check as an opt-in flag.

neha: great. i'll schedule a longer night-run with different tokenizers and report back.

jamie: logs and repro script here: https://internal.redwood/tools/kv-repro/long_ctx_stress.zip

perf-bot: [note] watchpoint set on kv_page.header.tag changes for PR D1234

oliver: if it gets stubborn after fixes we should also audit eviction path; maybe tombstone reuse isn't clearing headers consistently.

kate: agreed. add that to post-fix checklist.

jamie: closing loop for now — PR landed to main with conservative clear + test (D1234 -> merged). will re-run 100-run stress tomorrow morning and update thread.
